category_title: Students with learning difficulties and speech needs who engage through collaborative play and leadership roles
minimal_context: The student is reading a scene from A Midsummer Night's Dream and preparing to act it out in front of the class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please look at your copy of A Midsummer Night's Dream. We are going to read the text and then perform the scene in front of the class.

STUDENT: I don't know what these words mean. In the Mid summer night’s dream the text at first was quiet confusing.

TUTOR: Just keep reading and try your best. Who would like to volunteer to read the first character's lines?

STUDENT: Sometimes I feel comfortable because of the topic but sometimes I don’t like to raise my hand.

TUTOR: We need to move on to the drama activity now. Please stand up and perform your lines for the group.

STUDENT: I'm not doing it. Some people judge you... I just don’t like performing in front of people.

options.A: Speak to the student privately to have them reflect on the class and ask why they feel uncomfortable.
options.B: Explain the text in detail and frequently re-explain the meanings of individual lines and words to the class.
options.C: Provide the student with a choice between two different plotlines or potential dialogues for the scene.
options.D: Allow the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the audience for help.
